headline.purpose: The big chalked figure on each card (number, name, place).

title.purpose: Card headlines under the figure; lite chalk filter.

title-heavy.purpose: Cover card heading; side headings use it at 1.35rem.

statement.purpose: Cover sentence with true numbers inline at 800 / 1.55em.

caption.purpose: Card footers, hop caption, run details (tabular numerals).

shadows.name: print-on-pavement
shadows.purpose: Only under a raster object lying on the ground (share preview, rotated -1.5deg). Never on chalk.

motion.name: draw-in
motion.purpose: Chalk lines draw themselves when a card arrives; pre-drawn under reduced motion.

motion.name: card-settle
motion.purpose: Card arrival; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: chalk-hover
motion.purpose: Chalk button hover; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: Loading chalk loop in the status line only.

chalkFilters.name: chalk-line
chalkFilters.purpose: Drawn lines: displacement scale 3 plus dusty breakup.

chalkFilters.name: chalk-scrub
chalkFilters.purpose: Loose scrub strokes on slabs; heavy knock-out so pavement pits show.

chalkFilters.name: chalk-bed
chalkFilters.purpose: Dense under-layer beneath copy; small pits only.

chalkFilters.name: chalk-text-lite
chalkFilters.purpose: Titles, side headings, captions in the display face.

ground.texture: --aggregate: inline SVG of three fractal-noise layers (mottling, stones, white or dark speckle), 320px tile, per colour scheme

narrative.overview:
Your year of hangouts is drawn in chalk on the ground where it happened. The ground is pavement: sunlit pale concrete in light mode, charcoal asphalt with stone speckle in dark. Everything that is drawn (outlines, tallies, circled names, arrows, the year band, card fills, the hopscotch) is chalk, rendered as rough SVG strokes passed through turbulence filters so edges wobble and pavement pits show through. Nothing is a clean vector box, nothing glows, and nothing is a gradient.

The page is paged like a story, but the story is a hopscotch: numbered chalk squares on the left, the current one scrubbed in with chalk, and the current card at phone scale beside it. Each card is a chalked rectangle committed to one chalk colour, and that colour carries a mood when the card is about a mood. Hierarchy comes from scale in one display face, never from extra faces or decoration. Lines draw themselves in when a card arrives and are already drawn under reduced motion.

The world refuses the category default for year-in-review: full-bleed gradient story slides with giant neon numbers. It should feel like something a kid and a parent chalked after playing outside, not something built to keep you scrolling. Scope: this system covers the Wrapped app (`app/`). The product page (`docs/index.html`) is an older, separate surface that stays on its own plain style.
keyCharacteristics: Pavement ground with SVG-noise aggregate in both colour schemes; chalk does all the drawing.
Every outline is a hand-wobbled path through a chalk filter; no CSS borders on world elements.
Three mood chalks plus white and graphite chalk. Mood chalk always means a mood.
One display face (Bricolage Grotesque) with chalk-textured lettering; system UI for controls and body.
Hopscotch navigation as the signature interaction; arrows and keys work too.
Draw-in motion on arrival, fully pre-drawn under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Mood Chalk Rule
rules.body: Green, purple and yellow mean Let's hang, Quiet company and Busy, but wave, and nothing else. A slab, square, swatch or marker takes a mood chalk only when the data under it is that mood. Cards and squares with no mood are white chalk. A mood colour is always paired with the mood's name in text.

rules.name: The Same-Chalk Swatch Rule
rules.body: A mood swatch that sits on a slab of its own mood is scribbled in slab ink instead, so it never disappears into the slab.

rules.name: The Ground Is Pavement Rule
rules.body: The page background is always ground colour plus aggregate texture. Never a flat fill, a gradient, or a white page.

rules.name: The One Chalk Face Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is the only display face. Hierarchy comes from scale and weight, not from a second face or decorative styling.

rules.name: The Chalk Lettering Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type carry the heavier chalk-text filter; titles, side headings and captions in the display face carry the lite filter. System-UI text is never filtered.

rules.name: The Same-Ground Rule
rules.body: Chalk lies on the ground. It never casts a shadow and never floats above another layer.

dos: **Do** draw every outline and figure as a rough path through the chalk-line filter, sized to the element and seeded, so it never jumps on redraw.
**Do** commit each card to exactly one chalk: its mood's chalk if the card is about a mood, white chalk otherwise.
**Do** pair every mood colour with the mood's name in text.
**Do** keep the ground as ground colour plus aggregate texture in both colour schemes.
**Do** let chalk lines draw in on arrival (0.8s, cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)) and render them already drawn under prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** use Bricolage Grotesque for chalked lettering and system UI for controls and body, with hierarchy by scale.
donts: **Don't** use green, purple or yellow decoratively. They mean Let's hang, Quiet company and Busy, but wave.
**Don't** use full-bleed gradient story slides, giant neon numbers, or anything that reads as Spotify Wrapped.
**Don't** put CSS borders, border-radius boxes or drop shadows on chalk elements. Chalk lies flat on the ground.
**Don't** add a second display face or render display text without the chalk filter.
**Don't** show locations, maps or sharing on a kid's Wrapped.
